value: Study compares Yanomami/Brazil (n=15) with Yanomami/Venezuela (n=8), Matses (n=24), Tunapuco (n=12), and US urban group (n=44)
Shotgun metagenomic sequencing generated ~219 million reads total (~14 million per sample)
Taxonomic classification by Kraken; functional classification by SUPER-FOCUS
LEfSe analysis with Kruskal-Wallis test (alpha 0.05) and LDA score >4.0
Beta-diversity assessed using Bray-Curtis dissimilarity and PERMANOVA (999 permutations)
Ethics approval: Oswaldo Cruz Foundation Committee No. 638/11 and CONEP No. 16907

This paper is a microbiome characterization study of healthy traditional populations (Yanomami hunter-gatherers), not a clinical trial or disease treatment study. Most schema fields are not applicable.
Biomarker data refers to taxonomic markers (bacterial genera) distinguishing study groups, not clinical biomarkers for disease diagnosis or prognosis.

Paper reports sample size of n=15 for Yanomami/Brazil and compares with other groups (Yanomami/Venezuela n=8, Matses n=24, Tunapuco n=12, US n=44), but sample-level data not provided in the extracted text.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
The schema includes fields like 'tumor_size_residual_measurement' that are not applicable to this microbiome study, which does not involve oncology or tumor measurement.
No antibiotic exclusion criteria were explicitly stated in the study methods, though this is common practice in microbiome studies.

The paper does not explicitly state whether fecal samples were collected from participants at multiple timepoints or single timepoint; appears to be single timepoint based on 'A single stool sample was collected from each subject' but no temporal follow-up is mentioned.
